title: Evidence routing contract spec: RBACv2 ↔ SIEM export
summary: Working spec that defines the contract between vulnerability evidence producers (scanner pipelines, patch trackers) and consumers (SIEM, audit-store, remediation tracker) with RBACv2 decisioning in the middle. Goal: reliable, auditable export of vulnerability evidence enriched with RBAC-derived visibility, and consistent retention/rollback metadata for compliance audits.
background_and_problem_statement: We currently have multiple scanner outputs (SCA, SAST, dependency scanners) with different evidence shapes. SIEM ingest and our remediation UI both need a single canonical event shape and an authoritative visibility tag based on RBACv2 (team access + customer isolation). At present: missing fields, duplicate signals, and unclear ownership cause evidence loss during handoff and make SLA enforcement brittle.
goals: 1) Define canonical event fields for vuln evidence export to SIEM and audit-store. 2) Specify RBACv2 mapping rules to compute 'visibility' and 'ownership' attributes at export time. 3) Define retention and tamper-evident proof fields to support audits. 4) Provide a lightweight verification handshake between exporter and SIEM ingestion pipeline.
non_goals: Do not redesign scanner internals or change detection rules. This spec focuses on export/enrichment/contract, not remediation automation logic (except evidence tagging needed for rollbacks).
proposed_siem_event_schema_snippet: Flat field list (all strings unless noted): event_id | timestamp_utc | scanner_name | scanner_run_id | finding_id | severity | cve | package_name | package_version | repo_or_bucket | path | line_number | evidence_blob_url | first_seen | last_seen | exploitability_score | aggregator_confidence | raw_output_reference | rbac_visibility | owning_team | owning_owner_email | remediation_state | patch_due_date | proof_hash | proof_signature_ref
sample_event_example: event_id=evt-20260210-abc123; timestamp_utc=2026-02-10T14:12:34Z; scanner_name=oss-audit; scanner_run_id=run-57; finding_id=FND-9832; severity=high; cve=CVE-2025-9999; package_name=fast-serialize; package_version=2.1.4; repo_or_bucket=github.com/redwood/infra; path=/go/pkg/mod/...; line_number=73; evidence_blob_url=s3://evidence-prod/evt-2026-02-10-abc123.json; first_seen=2026-02-09T09:02:11Z; last_seen=2026-02-10T12:00:00Z; exploitability_score=7.1; aggregator_confidence=0.85; raw_output_reference=gs://scanner-raw/oss-audit/run-57/9832.json; rbac_visibility=team:eng-platform:read,team:sec:full; owning_team=eng-platform; owning_owner_email=rafael.gomez@redwood.com; remediation_state=triaged; patch_due_date=2026-02-24; proof_hash=sha256:3f5b...; proof_signature_ref=kms://redwood/proofs/evt-20260210-abc123
rbac_mapping_csv:
rbac_role,resource_pattern,visibility_level,derived_owner_team,notes
scanner-service,org/*:component/*,internal,eng-platform,service account exports default
sec-automation,shared/*,private,security,full visibility for security role
customer-sandbox,customer/*,restricted,customer-owner,restricted to customer tenant
cto-office,org/*,internal,exec-exceptions,only for exec audits
evidence_processing_flow: 1) Scanner finishes run and writes raw result to raw-bucket + emits an 'evidence-ready' message to pubsub. 2) Evidence-enricher pulls raw result, normalizes fields, computes aggregator_confidence, computes proof_hash, queries RBACv2 service for visibility/ownership, attaches rbac_visibility and owning_team. 3) Enricher writes canonical event to evidence-store (immutable) and emits SIEM-export message with handshake header (exporter_id + sequence + signature_ref). 4) SIEM-ingest validates signature_ref and sequence, acknowledges ingestion via pubsub ack channel. 5) If ingestion fails, enricher retries with exponential backoff and alerts on >3 failures to #sec-automation.
handshake_and_validation: Handshake = {exporter_id, export_sequence, signature_ref, timestamp}. Validation rules: sequence monotonic per exporter; signature_ref resolves to KMS-signed proof that includes event_id and proof_hash; SIEM must persist handshake record for traceability. If signature validation fails, SIEM should move event to quarantine index 'evidence_quarantine' and raise jira SEC-<auto-ticket>.
retention_and_audit_requirements: Retention: canonical evidence events retained 3 years in audit-store; SIEM index retention 1 year (fast index) + cold archive 3 years. Proofs (proof_hash + signature_ref) kept with canonical evidence. Tamper-evidence: store SHA-256 chain per day and publish daily digest to confluence-sec-audit (digest signed).
sla_and_escalation_matrix: Patch SLA mapping (for tracking only): critical=7 days, high=30 days, medium=90 days, low=180 days. Ownership escalation: 48h after assigned -> pager to owning_team on-call; 72h without ack -> auto-assign to security ops. All SLA misses generate auto jira SEC-SLA-xxxx linked to the canonical evidence event.
rollback_and_evidence_retention_notes: When a patch is reverted or a false positive is accepted, record rollback_event_id and rollback_reason on the canonical event and update remediation_state to 'rolled_back' or 'false_positive'. Retain original evidence and append a signed 'verdict' document (signed by owning_owner_email via KMS).
kpi_and_monitoring_suggestions:
- Export success rate (per exporter): target >= 99.5%
- Time from scanner run to canonical event <= 10 minutes for priority scanners
- Number of evidence_quarantine entries per week: target < 5
- SLA breach rate by severity: target < 1% monthly
open_questions:
- Do we want per-tenant obfuscation for customer PII in SIEM? (privacy tradeoff)
- Should RBACv2 evaluation happen in the enricher or deferred to SIEM (pros/cons in doc)
- How to handle aggregated findings across multiple repos (single canonical event vs multiple linked events)?
